name: Webnotics CRO Audit for WooCommerce
author: Webnotics

sections.description:
Webnotics CRO Audit looks at the pages of your store that you choose, the way a shopper sees them, and lists what may stop people from buying. Each finding has the evidence, its likely impact, the effort to fix it and a clear fix.

  • Only your own site is scanned. There is no box to enter another address.
  • Checkout and account pages are never opened.
  • The scanner identifies itself with its own user agent and follows your robots.txt.
  • Findings never compare your store with other stores, and your data is never used to train AI models.

The Free plan includes one home page audit in your first month. Paid plans scan 5, 20 or 100 pages a month, and extra pages can be bought as credits, valid for 365 days.

Run an audit from the CRO Audit menu in WordPress admin: choose the pages, follow the scan, and read the report with numbered marks on each screenshot. Pages that share one template are scanned once.

External services

Webnotics CRO Audit connects to an external audit service operated by Webnotics Pvt LTD, called Auditra. The service runs at https://croaudit.webnotics.solutions and performs the scans, so the plugin cannot audit a store without it. Nothing is sent to the service until you press Connect store and start an audit.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you press Connect store and start an audit: your site’s home URL is sent to the service. The service then reads a one time code from your site at /wp-json/auditra-cro/v1/challenge to confirm the plugin runs there, and returns an access key that is stored in your WordPress database.
  • When you open the CRO Audit menu: the access key is sent to read your plan, credits and audits. While a scan runs, the screen asks for progress every few seconds. Report screenshots are loaded from private links that expire after one hour.
  • When you save billing details: your name, email, address and optional GSTIN are sent to the service to make out GST invoices. Invoices are kept by the service as tax records, also after you disconnect.
  • When you buy a plan or credits, or press Manage subscription: the service creates a Stripe page and your browser goes to Stripe (stripe.com) to pay or manage the subscription. Card details go only to Stripe. Stripe terms: https://stripe.com/legal and privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • When you press Disconnect and delete data: the access key is sent, the service cancels an active subscription in Stripe, then deletes your audits, screenshots, plan, credits and billing details. It keeps the GST invoices (tax records) and, if you used the free home page audit, your domain and the date, so the free audit is given once per domain.
  • When you delete the plugin: nothing is sent. The key is removed from WordPress, and your account stays on the service, so connecting the same site again brings back your plan, credits and reports. Deleting the plugin does not cancel a subscription: use Manage subscription, or Disconnect and delete data.
  • When you press Get these fixed by Webnotics or Get this fixed in a report: your browser opens webnotics.org in a new tab with your site’s domain, the id of the audit and the numbers of the findings, so the form there is filled in for you. Nothing is sent unless you press it. It is a separate, paid service by Webnotics, and nothing is charged unless you ask for the work there. Its terms: https://webnotics.org/terms/ and privacy policy: https://webnotics.org/privacy-policy/
  • When you press Write a review: your browser opens wordpress.org in a new tab. The plugin stores your answer to the review question (Write a review, Later or Do not show again) in your WordPress user profile data and sends it nowhere.
  • When you run an audit: your browser talks only to your own site, which calls the service with the access key. The service visits the pages you chose, takes desktop and mobile screenshots and reads page text and structure. Screenshots and page text are sent to Anthropic (Claude) to write the findings, and are kept on the service until you disconnect. The addresses of up to three of the scanned pages are sent to Google PageSpeed Insights, which loads those pages itself to measure their speed. A site with no plugin activity for 90 days, and no active subscription, is deleted.

Terms and privacy policy of the service:

  • Terms of service: https://webnotics.org/cro-audit-for-woocommerce/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://webnotics.org/cro-audit-for-woocommerce/privacy-policy/

The service passes data to three other companies, as described above:

  • Stripe, for payments. Terms: https://stripe.com/legal and privacy policy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • Anthropic, for the analysis. Privacy policy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google PageSpeed Insights, for page speed. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce and this plugin.
  2. Make sure your site uses https and pretty permalinks (Settings, Permalinks, any option except Plain).
  3. Open CRO Audit in the WordPress admin menu. The screen checks https, permalinks and store visibility for you.
  4. Press Connect store and start an audit, then choose the pages to scan.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free?

Yes. The plugin is free to install, and the Free plan includes one home page audit in your first month, with desktop and mobile results. To audit more pages, choose a paid plan: Starter (5 pages a month), Growth (20 pages a month) or Scale (100 pages a month). Extra pages can be bought as credits that stay valid for 365 days. Pages are charged only when their scan finishes.

Which pages can I audit?

Any public page of your own store that you choose: the home page, product pages, category pages, the cart, and other pages and blog posts. Pages that share one template are scanned once, so you do not pay twice for the same layout. The scanner never opens checkout or account pages and never places an order.

Is my store data safe?

The audit only reads the pages you select, as a shopper would see them. Screenshots and page text are sent to Anthropic (Claude) to write the findings, and are kept until you disconnect. Your data is never used to train AI models, and your store is never compared with other stores. You can delete your audits, screenshots, plan, credits and billing details at any time with Disconnect and delete data. Invoices are kept as tax records. See the External services section for the full list of what is sent and when.

What do I get in the report?

Numbered findings marked on your own desktop and mobile screenshots. Each finding has the evidence, the likely impact, the effort to fix it and a clear fix. The findings with high impact and low effort are listed first, in the Start here box of the report.

Why does it need https and pretty permalinks?

The service confirms your site by reading a one time code from your site’s REST API at /wp-json/. That address only exists with pretty permalinks, and the check only runs over https.

What happens when I delete and reinstall the plugin?

Nothing is lost. Deleting the plugin only removes its key from WordPress. Install it again and press Connect: the same site gets back its plan, subscription, credits, billing details and reports. To delete your data, press Disconnect and delete data before you delete the plugin.

Does WordPress have to be at the root of the domain?

Yes, for now. Sites in a sub folder (for example example.com/shop/wp) cannot be connected yet.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Report: Get these fixed by Webnotics in the Start here box, and Get this fixed under each finding. Both open a paid fixing service on webnotics.org in a new tab. Nothing is sent unless you press them.
  • A small box on the plugin’s screens asks for a review on WordPress.org after you have opened a finished report. Later hides it for 14 days. Do not show again hides it for good.
  • Free plan: a box under the report lists the paid plans, with pages and price a month, and a link to Billing.
  • Connect: a failing https, domain root or permalinks check has a Why is this needed? link to the questions and answers.

1.0.1

  • New short description and tags on the plugin’s WordPress.org page.
  • Screenshot 7 shows the Start here list of quick wins.
  • CSV downloads are named webnotics-cro-audits and webnotics-cro-invoices.
  • The plugin’s home page and its Terms and Privacy links are on webnotics.org.
  • The readme and the footer of the plugin’s screens name the external service the plugin connects to.

1.0.0

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • Older development releases are listed in changelog.txt.
